title: Authorization Workflows and Travel Templates — Operational Guide
author: Maya Singh
content:
Overview
========

Purpose: This page defines standardized authorization workflows, approval thresholds, vendor onboarding steps, travel approval templates, and associated operational procedures for Redwood Inference. It is intended for employees, managers, finance, security, and platform teams who participate in access approvals, change management, procurement, vendor management, and corporate travel.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood entities worldwide and covers: access & permissions requests; change approvals for infra and application deployments; procurement & expense approvals; vendor onboarding & renewals; and company-sponsored travel bookings and reimbursements.

Ownership
---------
- Document owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team)
- Primary contributors: Security (IAM), Eng-SRE, People Ops, Procurement
- Stakeholders: Product, Eng-Platform, Customer Success

Quick links
-----------
- Access request form (IAM Service): https://console.redwood.internal/iam/requests
- Procurement system (ProcureFlow): https://procureflow.redwood.internal
- Vendor onboarding (VendorHub): https://vendorhub.redwood.internal
- Expense system (ExpenseTrack): https://expenses.redwood.internal

1) Roles and responsibilities
----------------------------
- Requester: initiates requests (access, change, purchase, travel).
- Manager/Team Lead: verifies business justification and approves up to their approval limit.
- Security/IAM: verifies least-privilege assignments, performs risk review for privileged access.
- Procurement: validates vendor contracts, PO issuance, and vendor financial checks.
- Finance: verifies budget availability and final reimbursement.
- Legal: reviews non-standard contract terms, NDAs, data processing agreements.

2) Access & permissions workflow
--------------------------------
Principles: least privilege, role-based assignments, short-lived elevated access, auditability.

Access tiers:
- Tier 0 — Public/Read-only: no approval required for public docs.
- Tier 1 — Standard user: manager approval within 48 hours SLA.
- Tier 2 — Elevated (service accounts, admin console): manager + IAM review, 72-hour SLA.
- Tier 3 — Sensitive & Privileged (KMS keys, production DB write): manager + IAM + Security + VP signoff, 7-day SLA.

Request process (standard):
1. Requester files a request in IAM Service with justification, scope, and duration.
2. Manager reviews and either approves or returns for clarification within 48 hours.
3. For Tier 2/3, IAM performs a risk check and documents exceptions in the audit log.
4. Provisioning automation (when available) creates the account/role and notifies Requester.
5. Access is automatically time-limited; renewal requests follow the same workflow.

Elevated access checklist (for approvers):
- Business justification clearly stated and linked to ticket or JIRA.
- Access duration <= 30 days unless approved as recurring.
- Principle of least privilege applied (no 'owner' role unless necessary).
- MFA enabled and device compliance validated via Intune or device inventory.

Automated controls and SLAs:
- IAM Service will auto-expire temporary access at the end of the requested window.
- SLA targets: standard requests 48 hours, elevated 72 hours, privileged 7 days.
- Weekly orphaned-account report produced to eng-sre@redwood.internal.

3) Change management (infra & app changes)
-----------------------------------------
Change tiers and approval matrix:
| Tier | Impact | Examples | Approvers | Typical lead time | Rollback SLA |
|------|--------|----------|----------|------------------:|------------:|
| C1   | Low    | Config tweak, non-prod deploy | Team lead | 0–24h | 30m |
| C2   | Medium | Production bugfix, schema migration (non-destructive) | Team lead + Eng-SRE | 24–72h | 60m |
| C3   | High   | Version upgrades, DB migrations, infra changes | Eng-SRE + Product + Security | 72h+ | 30m guaranteed |

Pre-change checklist (must be attached to change ticket):
- Rollback procedure documented and tested.
- Monitoring playbook with key metrics and alert thresholds (latency, error-rate, CPU).
- Stakeholder notification list (SLACK channel, oncall).
- Scheduled maintenance window (if customer-facing).

Change execution steps (standard):
1. Create change ticket in ChangeBoard with planned window, impact, approvals, rollback plan.
2. Run preflight smoke tests in staging; attach logs.
3. Execute during approved window with one engineer owning runbook.
4. Monitor metrics and escalate to oncall per runbook if thresholds exceeded.
5. Close ticket with post-change summary and incident link if any anomalies occurred.

Emergency changes:
- Emergency changes require Eng-SRE + incident commander signoff post-facto; must be documented within 24 hours.

4) Data classification and handling
---------------------------------
Data classes:
- Public: safe to publish.
- Internal: Redwood internal use; no PII.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, or proprietary models.
- Restricted: regulated data subject to contractual or legal restrictions.

Handling rules by class:
- Encryption at rest via KMS required for Confidential and Restricted.
- Access limited to Tier 2/3 and logged.
- Backups encrypted and stored in region-specific buckets matching data residency requirements.

Data retention & deletion:
- Retention baseline: logs 90 days, backups 180 days, product telemetry 2 years (unless contract specifies otherwise).
- Data deletion requests must follow the Data Subject Request SOP (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-subject-requests).

5) Procurement, expenses, and approval thresholds
------------------------------------------------
Approval thresholds (examples):
- <= $1,000: Manager approval via ProcureFlow.
- $1,001–$25,000: Manager + Procurement review.
- $25,001–$250,000: Director + Procurement + Finance.
- > $250,000: VP + Legal + Procurement + CFO approval.

Procurement workflow (vendor purchase):
1. Requester creates a requisition in ProcureFlow with business justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement validates vendor, performs legal/financial checks and obtains quotes if required.
3. Finance verifies budget availability and issues PO.
4. Vendor receives PO and onboarding begins via VendorHub.

Expense policy (travel & misc):
- Use ExpenseTrack to submit receipts within 10 business days of expense.
- Per-diem and policy caps: domestic lodging up to $275/night unless pre-approved; international per-diem per country schedule in ExpenseTrack guidelines.
- Unauthorized spend (personal entertainment, family members, luxury upgrades) is not reimbursable without prior approval.

6) Vendor onboarding & lifecycle
------------------------------
Vendor onboarding minimum requirements:
- Completed VendorHub intake form and company W-9 or local equivalent.
- Proof of insurance (if applicable), references, and SOC2 or equivalent report for vendors handling Confidential/Restricted data.
- Signed MSA and applicable DPA/Privacy Addendum reviewed by Legal.

Vendor risk tiers and controls:
- Low risk: commodity vendors (office supplies) — ProcureFlow + basic vetting.
- Medium risk: SaaS vendors with internal access — SOC2 assessment and Standard Contract.
- High risk: vendors with access to customer data or production systems — Security questionnaire + on-site review + encrypted connection requirements.

Contract renewal checklist:
- Contract expiration notice triggers 90/60/30-day reminders to vendor owner.
- Renewal requires business justification, cost analysis, and Security re-assessment for data-handling changes.

7) Travel policy and approval templates
-------------------------------------
Purpose: Ensure safe, cost-effective travel with clear approval and reimbursement paths.

Pre-approval requirements:
- All business travel must be pre-approved in TravelBoard (link: https://travelboard.redwood.internal) with estimated cost and budget code.
- Manager approval required for trips <= 5 days. Director approval required for international travel or trips > 5 days.

Standard travel booking guidelines:
- Use company travel partners for flights and hotels when available.
- Economy or premium-economy for flights under 8 hours; manager approval needed for upgrades.
- Use company-preferred hotels; exceptions require explanation.

Travel approval template (copy into TravelBoard comments):
"Trip purpose: [brief business objective]
Dates: [start] to [end]
Estimated cost: $[amount]
Budget code: [code]
Business justification: [1–2 sentences]
Risk considerations: [health/visa/travel advisories]
Approvals: Manager: [name], Director: [name if required]"

Emergency travel and evacuation:
- People Ops maintains an emergency travel roster and will coordinate evacuation or emergency support for employees in high-risk regions. Contact emergency@redwood.internal.

8) Templates and sample artifacts
--------------------------------
Include these templates in the page attachments and in Template Library:
- Access request template (IAM): fields: requester, resource, duration, justification, JIRA link.
- Change ticket template (ChangeBoard): fields: scope, impact, rollback, test plan, owner, stakeholders.
- Purchase requisition template (ProcureFlow): vendor, SKU, justification, budget code, preferred PO terms.
- Travel approval template (see above).

Sample access request (IAM) payload:
```
{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.internal",
  "resource": "prod-db-write",
  "tier": "3",
  "duration_days": "7",
  "justification": "Emergency data fix for customer-123 outage",
  "jira": "ENG-10234"
}
```

9) Escalation matrix and SLAs
----------------------------
- Access request SLAs: Standard 48h / Elevated 72h / Privileged 7 days.
- Procurement turnarounds: low-risk purchases <= 5 business days; complex contracts 30–60 business days.
- Change rollback SLA: 30–60 minutes depending on tier.

Escalation contacts (primary):
- Security (IAM): iam-support@redwood.internal
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.internal
- Finance: finance-ops@redwood.internal
- People Ops (travel/emergency): peopleops@redwood.internal

10) Audit, reporting, and continuous improvement
----------------------------------------------
- Quarterly access reviews performed by IAM and team leads; results reported to Security Council.
- Procurement and vendor spend report monthly to Finance with variance analysis.
- Post-mortems for failed changes or procurement disputes documented and linked to this page.

Appendix A — Approval matrix (table)
-----------------------------------
| Request type | Primary approver | Secondary approver | Notes |
|--------------|------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Access Tier 1 | Manager | IAM (audit) | Auto-approved after manager signoff |
| Access Tier 2 | Manager | IAM + Security | Risk review required |
| Purchase <$1k | Manager | Procurement (notify) | Budget must exist |
| Purchase $1k–$25k | Manager | Procurement + Finance | 2 competitive quotes for software > $10k |
| Travel domestic | Manager | People Ops | Use TravelBoard |

Appendix B — Change window checklist (copy for runbook)
------------------------------------------------------
1. Preflight: backup snapshots, runbook owner assigned, notify oncall.
2. Execute: one step at a time, validate metrics after each step.
3. Monitor: 30m at minimum post-change observation.
4. Rollback: execute rollback steps immediately if critical thresholds hit.
5. Close: document outcomes and update incident/change ticket.
